messages.subject: Why is model-block never entered?
parts:
I have a case where a model runs without ever entering the model block; simplified:


transformed parameter{
  print("Transformed")
}


model {
  #x~ y etc
  print("Model")
#  for (i ...) {  } etch
}



Under rstan, the print statement in the transformed block prints on every iteration, but the model-print is never executed, and the iterations flush through in fractions of a second, all with NA and Inf results, but terminates without errors.

Why is the model block is never entered? This is a slight modification of a successfully running program, after replacing individual coefficients by a vector of coefficient.

If required, I can try to boil down the whole code, but possibly it's something absolutely trivial.

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Why is model-block never entered?
parts:
There are two issues.

1. Your init values don't work. If I use init=0, everything works
and you get finite lp__ and parameter values. In general, Stan
does a pretty good job initializing itself.

2. There's also a bug in print() in the current version of RStan that
suppresses printing in the model. That will be fixed in the next
release. Sorry about that.
